I'm noting an important discrepancy: the flag toggle was inferred from logs, but the flag provider history actually showed zero recent flag changes, so that's an assumption worth flagging. Also, since the incident hasn't recovered, the duration should be treated as a lower bound, and no mitigation was actually applied yet—only a draft PR was opened. I should be careful not to present inferred figures as if they were directly computed values.

Root cause boils down to the monthly-spend-feature flag being enabled at 21:49, which exposed an unguarded division in the spend summary code, causing a ZeroDivisionError for account page requests. My executive summary should avoid naming specific components, describing it instead as the account page failing for shoppers after a new spending-summary feature switched on. I'll keep the root cause field to just one or two sentences, listing the key assumptions clearly: the flag change is inferred from log evaluation counts (not confirmed by the provider), the zero-spend divisor is inferred from the code path rather than verified, and no deploy or config changes were found in the checked windows.

assumptions: The incident was still ongoing at the last minute of metrics available, so the stated duration and all impact figures are lower bounds derived from a truncated window, not measurements of the full event.

The feature flag toggle at 21:49 is inferred from the service's own log lines (evaluation counts moving from 'off - 200' to 'off 33 / on 167' to 'on - 200'). The flag provider's own change history was queried and reported zero recent flag changes, so the toggle is not corroborated by the system of record; that discrepancy has not been explained.

That the flag flip caused the errors is a correlation in time plus a matching stack trace, not a tested hypothesis - no mitigation was ever attempted, so the causal link was never confirmed by turning the flag back off.
The specific trigger for the division by zero (a shopper with a zero spend total) is read off the code path named in the stack trace; it was not verified against actual request data.
Absence of a deploy or config cause rests on the change-event queries returning zero results for the windows checked; it assumes that feed is complete for this service.
The three investigation passes read overlapping copies of the same log and metric data; the repeated evidence is duplication of one observation, not independent confirmation.
The 0.03 hours Argus held the incident measures automated response time only and says nothing about how long the service was broken.
input.executive_summary: Starting at 21:49 UTC on 28 September 2026, the account page of the online shop began failing for a large share of shoppers who tried to load it. The cause was a newly switched-on spending-summary feature that crashed while calculating a shopper's monthly totals. Automated monitoring raised an alert about five minutes after the failures began, and the automated responder investigated three times over roughly a minute and a half. It correctly identified the newly enabled feature as the cause but had no safe action available to it, so it took no corrective action at all; instead it opened a draft code change for a human engineer to review and escalated the incident. The service was still failing at the last moment for which we have data, so the outage window recorded here is a floor, not a final duration, and every impact figure quoted elsewhere is bounded the same way. Nothing was changed in production during the response, and no data was lost - the effect on shoppers was failed account page loads while the feature remained on.
input.root_cause: At 21:49 UTC the 'monthly-spend-feature' flag went from off to on for io-shop (ramping over 21:49-21:50), which put an unguarded division in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 into the request path; account page requests that hit it raised ZeroDivisionError, and the error rate jumped from its ~1% baseline at exactly that minute. No deploy or config change appeared in the change windows the investigator checked (114 and 414 minutes back), so the flag flip is the only change lined up with the onset.
